Logan —
I reviewed the redline. High-level legal position and suggested edits are in the attached counter (Redwood_Counter_0829.pdf). Key recommendations below: 

1) Pricing ladder (down-steps): Acceptable only if we add a "stability credit" clause — if customer reduces consumption within the first 6 months after committing to a higher tier, they receive a one-time credit equal to the difference in fees, capped at the onboarding discount (see §3.2). This protects Redwood from churn-triggered revenue loss.

2) True-up window: We cannot agree to locking reconciliations to a two-quarter window for initial contract years. Proposed compromise: two-quarter true-up permitted during a 12-month probation (first year) but require annual true-up thereafter. This reduces operational churn while being responsive to Cobalt's ramping concern.

3) Onboarding discount: We can offer a limited 10% onboarding discount for months 1-3, but (a) it must be applied as a one-time invoice credit (not lowering list price), and (b) must not stack with other promotional credits or future retrospective adjustments. Add explicit non-stacking language.

4) Cap/Floor guardrails: The order form should include a price floor equal to 70% of the effective list rate to avoid irrationally low per-token pricing and a price cap tied to an agreed maximum per-token rate in high-usage months. Also include a minimum monthly commitment clause for months 4-6 if they want aggressive ladder drops.

5) Billing & Audit: Add a standard audit right (30 days notice) and require that any refund/credit calculation be reconciled with Redwood's billing ledger export format; define dispute resolution timeframe (30 days).

6) Termination for pricing variance: If discounts and retro adjustments reduce realized ARR by more than 20% compared to committed ARR for two consecutive quarters, Redwood may suspend promotional benefits until stabilized.

Please see comments in the attached PDF for exact redline snippets. I flagged language that could be ambiguous and proposed more precise definitions ("true-up period", "effective month", "onboarding credit").

If Sales wants to push harder on two-quarter true-ups, we can handle that as a commercial concession in exchange for a higher minimum commitment and a shorter notice period for price escalations.

-Laura
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
